validateCertificate(bytes).details: This function MUST NOT revert. It should return false for malformed or invalid certificates.      The security model requires that the prover's validity claim matches what this function returns.      If they disagree (e.g., prover claims valid but this returns false), the OSP will revert.      The proof format is: [certSize(8), certificate, claimedValid(1), validityProof...]      The validityProof section can contain additional verification data such as:      - Cryptographic signatures      - Merkle proofs      - Timestamped attestations      - Or other authentication mechanisms

params.proof: The proof data starting with [certSize(8), certificate, validityProof...]

returns.isValid: True if the certificate is valid, false otherwise

params.certHash: The keccak256 hash of the certificate (from machine's proven state)
params.offset: The offset into the preimage to read from (from machine's proven state)
params.proof: The proof data starting with [certSize(8), certificate, customData...]

returns.preimageChunk: The 32-byte chunk of preimage data at the specified offset

validateCertificate(bytes).notice: Validates whether a certificate is well-formed and legitimate

validateReadPreimage(bytes32,uint256,byt.notice: Validates a custom DA proof and returns the preimage chunk
